newsitem.title: UK: EU seen awarding up to 50,000 T sugar at tender.
newsitem.headline: EU seen awarding up to 50,000 T sugar at tender.

text.p: The European Union (EU) is expected to award up to 50,000 tonnes of current series white sugar at its weekly tender later on Wednesday, traders said.
"The tonnage will probably be quite small, probably not less than 20,000 tonnes but certainly not more than 50,000 tonnes this week," said one trader.
"It sounds like there's going to be quite a small volume," said another.
This week's maximum restitution level was estimated at between 43.085 and 43.105 Ecus (European currency units) per 100 kilos of sugar based on the spot August Matif contract.
Last week the EU awarded 34,500 tonnes in its tender at a maximum rebate of 43.069 Ecus.
Licences are currently valid until the end of September as the EU does not normally permit validity to extend into the new campaign.
The EU is still lagging behind its sugar export target for 1996/97 and also last year's cumulative exports, traders said.
